newsitem.title: USA: U.S. State Dept has recommendations on Iran, Libya.
newsitem.headline: U.S. State Dept has recommendations on Iran, Libya.

text.p: The U.S. State Department has approved recommendations set to go to the White House to carry out the Iran-Libya sanctions law that went into effect two months ago, an administration official said Wednesday.

The recommendations call for the State Department to enforce the law, which requires the United States to slap sanctions on anyone who invests $40 million or more in any one year in oil and gas projects in Iran or Libya, and penalize anyone who violates U.N. embargoes on Libya.
Normally the Treasury Department carries out sanctions rules.
The U.S. official declined to disclose the recommendations made on how to interpret the law.
No decisions have been made on whether it applies to Turkey or Malaysia, which both signed oil and gas agreements with Iran in August.
U.S. officials are still collecting information on those deals, the source said.

The administration plans to hold a public briefing on the guidelines probably "in the next month or so," the official said, adding: "There's going to have to be agreement on the guidelines before we have a briefing."
